reason: E1 directly supports Hf-rich phase precipitation at interfaces and its role in hindering grain boundary sliding/dislocation movement, improving high-temperature strength and ductility in a similar dual-phase HEA. E2 establishes the baseline corrosion vulnerability of AlCoCrFeNi2.1, particularly at B2 phase interfaces, but provides no evidence that Hf addition improves corrosion resistance or room-temperature creep. The premise that interface precipitates enhance corrosion resistance is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Hf addition precipitates Hf-rich phases at interfaces in dual-phase HEAs
Hf-rich phases hinder grain boundary sliding and dislocation movement
